chapters.summary: The Preacher laments that life is vanity, all things move in endless cycles, there is nothing new under the sun, and all our toil is without profit.
keyPoints: The Preacher declares that all things are vanity, and man's toil under the sun brings nothing new.
Nature moves in endless cycles and generations come and go, yet nothing achieved is lasting.
Even wisdom and knowledge bring sorrow, for in much wisdom is much grief.
chapters.application: We often chase achievement and pleasure, but we should recognize their fleeting vanity and instead seek what is eternal—giving thanks in the ordinary and building our lives on the fear of God.

chapters.summary: The Preacher tests pleasure, wealth, and labor, and finds them all to be vanity; only the fear of God brings true satisfaction in life.
keyPoints: The Preacher pursues pleasure and laughter, only to find them vanity.
Building great works and amassing wealth still cannot bring lasting satisfaction.
Both wisdom and folly end in vanity, for all the fruit of one's labor must at last be left to another.
chapters.application: Do not place your hope in things that pass away. Give thanks each day for God's provision, receive the fruit of your labor with a reverent heart, and remember to walk with God.

chapters.summary: There is a time and season for everything, but God has set eternity in the human heart, so that people would fear him.
keyPoints: To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven—a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to pluck up what is planted.
God has made everything beautiful in its time, and he has set eternity in the human heart.
God will judge the righteous and the wicked alike, for all our toil and every deed lies in his hand.
chapters.application: Facing the different seasons of life, let us submit to God's ordering of our days and find joy in doing good even amid our labor, for there is a time for everything, and God holds tomorrow in his hands.

chapters.summary: This chapter examines the oppression, toil, and loneliness found in life, and points to the value of companionship and contentment.
keyPoints: The oppressed have no comforter, and this is more grievous than death itself—so that the dead are counted more fortunate than the living.
Both toil and envy are vanity; better a quiet handful than two hands full of labor and a chasing after the wind.
Two are better than one, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken, showing the importance of companionship and mutual support.
chapters.application: In the midst of a busy life, learn contentment; treasure those around you and support one another, guarding against loneliness and envy, and receive the present moment with a thankful heart.

chapters.summary: This chapter teaches us to guard our words and keep our vows before God, showing that wealth is vanity and that the secret of true satisfaction lies in the fear of God.
keyPoints: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God, for to draw near and listen is better than the sacrifice of fools.
Pay what you vow to God, for it is better not to vow at all than to vow and not fulfill it, lest his anger be kindled.
Wealth gained by labor ends in vanity; only the one who fears God can truly enjoy what he has.
chapters.application: Come before God with a reverent heart, guard your words, and keep the vows you make; at the same time, receive your daily bread from his hand with gratitude, and be content.

chapters.summary: The Preacher points out that if a person has wealth but cannot enjoy it, this too is vanity; and no one can dispute with God, for life is fleeting as a shadow.
keyPoints: For a person to have riches yet not be able to enjoy them is a grievous evil—like a stillborn child, who comes in vanity and departs in darkness.
Even one who lives a thousand years twice over but never enjoys any good ends up no better than that child, a fate that leaves us sighing.
No one can contend with God, for his power is supreme; all our labor is but for our mouths, yet our hearts remain unsatisfied.
chapters.application: Treasure the present and give thanks for what you have, rather than fretting over what you lack. Seek God in the midst of your labor and learn contentment, for life is short, and only the fear of God brings true satisfaction.

chapters.summary: The Preacher teaches that wisdom is better than folly, urging us to face life honestly, fear God, and avoid all extremes.
keyPoints: A good name is better than precious ointment, and the day of death is better than the day of birth.
Wisdom gives the wise more strength than ten rulers in a city, yet no one is free from sin.
Do not be overly righteous, nor be overly wicked; whoever fears God will avoid both extremes.
chapters.application: Give thanks in times of prosperity and reflect in times of adversity; avoid extremes and pride, keep a reverent heart always, and rely on God through each day.

chapters.summary: This chapter examines wisdom and submission to authority, showing that in the face of an unpredictable and unjust world, fearing God and holding fast to wisdom is the surest way to live.
keyPoints: Wisdom makes a person's face shine and softens a hard countenance, showing how precious wisdom is.
Obey the king's command, knowing that God will judge in the end; wisdom gives a person discernment of the proper time and way.
Though the wicked may prosper and the righteous may suffer, those who fear God will surely be blessed in the end, while emptiness and wickedness will not last.
chapters.application: Facing a world full of uncertainty and injustice, live with wisdom, fear God, and keep to your calling, trusting firmly that he will judge in the end—so that even in hardship you may still hold on to peace and hope.

chapters.summary: The Preacher says that in the face of death, wisdom and folly make no difference; while we live, we should enjoy the grace God gives and faithfully fulfill our calling.
keyPoints: The righteous and the wise share the same fate as the wicked, yet their lives are in God's hand.
The dead know nothing and receive no more reward, so those who are alive should treasure this present life.
Wisdom is better than strength, yet a single sinner can destroy much good.
chapters.application: Treasure today, work faithfully, and enjoy the blessings God has given, for death is the destination of every person—but God remains our refuge.

chapters.summary: Through contrasting wisdom and folly, this chapter teaches us to act with humility, and points out the folly sometimes found among rulers and the consequences of careless words.
keyPoints: As dead flies give perfume a foul smell, so a little folly can outweigh wisdom and honor.
The wise give careful thought to their steps, while the fool's reckless words bring trouble on himself.
Folly is often found among those in power, but wisdom helps a person navigate injustice and crisis.
chapters.application: In daily life and work, clothe yourself with humility, guard your words, and rely on the wisdom God gives, so as to avoid the harm that folly brings.

chapters.summary: Ecclesiastes 11 urges us to give generously and work diligently even amid uncertainty, and to remember our Creator while we are still young.
keyPoints: Do good generously, and do not withhold it because the future is uncertain, for God will surely provide.
Remember your Creator while you are young, before the days of trouble come.
Life is vanity and full of the unknown, so seize the moment and faithfully do the work before you.
chapters.application: Even amid uncertainty, keep doing good and working diligently, and fear God while you are young, for life is short and we are meant to live for eternity.

chapters.summary: The Preacher urges the young to remember their Creator while they are still young, describes the scenes of old age and death, and finally concludes that the whole duty of man is to fear God and keep his commandments.
keyPoints: Urges the young to remember God while they are young, before the days of trouble come.
Depicts the decline of old age and the certainty of death, when life fades like a lamp going out.
Sums up the message of the whole book: to fear God and keep his commandments is the whole duty of man.
chapters.application: While it is still today, remember God and treasure your time, living each day in reverence, for God will bring every deed into judgment.
